# Variable Types {.unnumbered}

::: {.content-visible when-profile="stata"}
{{< video https://youtu.be/WWTpSJZkZcw >}}

## Key concepts/commands:

1.  numeric variables: many different specific numeric types, but they are shown in black or blue in the Data Editor

2.  string variables: these are text (non-numeric) variables, and they are shown in red in the Data Editor

3.  `codebook`: show variable information, including the numeric values underlying any "value labels" (for variables showing up in blue)

    ```         
    codebook u_fam
    ```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="r"}
{{< video https://youtu.be/xxr3Rc6P2Vo >}}

## Model script

``` r
install.packages("rio")
library(rio)
data <- import("https://learndata.net/binge.Rds", trust = TRUE)
str(data)
levels(data$sex_factor)
```

## Key concepts/syntax:

1.  numeric variables: often indicated as `num` for short, there are many different specific numeric types

2.  character variables: often indicated as `chr` for short, these are text (non-numeric) variables, also known as *string* variables

3.  factor variables: sometimes indicated as `fct` for short, these are qualitative variables that take on specific levels (which can be text) from a finite list

4.  `import()`: flexible command for loading data files, using the `rio`` package

    ``` r
    data <- import("https://learndata.net/binge.Rds", trust = TRUE)
    ```

5.  `str()`: show the variable type for each variable in a dataset

    ``` r
    str(data)
    ```

6.  `levels()`: show the levels of a factor variable

    ``` r
    levels(data$sex_factor)
    ```
:::
